advisor_identified: Lisa Wynne Smith, historian of gender and medicine; University of Saskatchewan (2002–2015), then University of Essex; co-supervisor of Erin Spinney.

doctorate.title: Women’s health care in England and France (1650–1775)

evidence.says: The university repository record for Erin Spinney’s 2018 Naval and Military Nursing in the British Empire c. 1763–1830 lists Lisa Smith and Matthew Neufeld as advisors.
Her faculty biography states that she worked in Saskatchewan’s History Department from 2002 to 2015 and returned to Essex in September 2015. Qualifications list a Ph.D., University of Essex (2002).
Sally Ann Osborn’s thesis, bibliography p. 411, identifies Lisa Wynne Smith’s Women’s health care in England and France (1650–1775) as a 2002 PhD thesis at the University of Essex.
Katherine A. Walker, Pain and Surgery in England, circa 1620–circa 1740, footnote 10, cites the same title and author as an Essex PhD dissertation, but dates it 2001.

notes: The linked 2011 Akron dissertation, Netta Taylor and the Divided Ohio Home Front, 1861–65, does not match her Essex doctorate. Year follows her institutional qualifications and Osborn’s bibliography; Walker gives 2001. Title is established through scholarly citations; no direct thesis catalogue record was located.
